clue.text: One worn kilt has come apart

indicators.note: something that has come apart is in pieces, so the letters of the preceding words are reassembled

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's ancient kilt has finally fallen to bits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One worn' is the definition: something worn on the head. The kilt is pure misdirection towards Scottish dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A top hat of glossy silk is a garment, something a gentleman puts on his head.

clue.text: Magnificent national university with power installed

indicators.note: the university and power letters are installed inside the national

parts.note: a Serb is a national of Serbia
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A splendid national university that has had a generator fitted.
explanation.definitionFit: Superb is a synonym meaning excellent or splendid in the highest degree.

clue.text: Fighting duke with general on side of sailors

indicators.note: in a down entry, the general sits on top of the fighting duke

parts.note: Robert E Lee was the Confederate general
war is fighting

explanation.surface: A battling duke and a general fighting alongside the navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors speak of the side sheltered from the wind as the lee, the opposite of windward.

clue.text: Crippled animal lacking energy and another rising

indicators.note: lacking means the energy letter is taken out of the animal

parts.note: a hamster is a small pet animal
E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means this word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a gnu is another animal, a wildebeest

explanation.surface: A lame creature, short of energy, beside another one getting to its feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a hamstrung animal has its leg tendons cut, so it is disabled or crippled.

clue.text: Can agent finally provide work for coiffeuse?

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word agent

explanation.surface: Could an employment agent find a hairdresser some work?
explanation.walkthrough: A coiffeuse is a female hairdresser.
explanation.definitionFit: Colouring a client's hair is a typical job a hairdresser carries out.

clue.text: Letters secure after going to front

indicators.note: tells us the word for 'after', printed second, is moved to the front

parts.note: post- is a prefix meaning after
to bag something is to secure or capture it

explanation.surface: Someone fastening something tightly after moving to the front of a queue.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'secure' then 'after', and 'going to front' puts the second of these first.
explanation.definitionFit: A postbag is the collection of mail received, so it stands for letters as a body.

clue.text: Extremely popular artist with piles? More or less

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: William Etty was an English painter
piles of something means much of it

explanation.surface: A hugely successful painter with haemorrhoids? Well, almost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like an intensifier for popular, but takes that word's ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretty much is an informal phrase meaning almost or nearly, just as more or less does.

clue.text: Letter opener found next to radio

definitions.meaning: the vapour from a kettle softens envelope glue, so it can open mail secretly
in the old phrase ... radio, a jocular term for broadcast sound radio, this word comes just before radio

explanation.walkthrough: 'Steam radio' is a British joking term for old-fashioned sound radio, as opposed to television.
explanation.definitionFit: Kettle vapour unseals envelopes, and the word sits before 'radio' in a familiar British phrase.

clue.text: Bobtailed horse greeting airlines

indicators.note: a bobtailed creature has its tail docked, so the horse loses its final letter

parts.note: a bronco is a wild horse
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A horse with a docked tail welcomes passengers from an air carrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'airlines' is not carriers but air passages, read as air lines.
explanation.definitionFit: The bronchi are the tubes carrying breath from the windpipe to the lungs.

clue.text: Sea creature not closing large eyes when swimming

indicators.note: letters that are swimming are moving about, so they are rearranged
not closing means the word large loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A marine animal swimming with its big eyes wide open.
explanation.definitionFit: A large seal of North Atlantic coasts, a marine mammal common around Britain.

clue.text: Broadcast opened with items from Italy

indicators.note: to broadcast seed is to scatter it, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A radio programme that began with a selection of Italian news items.
explanation.definitionFit: Piedmont is a region of north-west Italy, so a Piedmontese thing comes from that country.

clue.text: Horace's work in recital not paid for

indicators.note: something said in a recital is spoken out, so we want a word sounding like another

parts.note: a debt still owed has not been paid for

explanation.surface: A recital of Latin verse that nobody paid to attend.
explanation.walkthrough: Horace, the Roman poet, wrote the Odes.
explanation.definitionFit: Horace's best-known poems are lyric pieces of that form, so one of them is an example of his work.

clue.text: Singer from Providence's business area

indicators.note: the singer comes from the state, so the state's letters lead

parts.note: Providence is the capital of Rhode Island, abbreviated RI
an alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice

explanation.surface: A vocalist from Providence, Rhode Island, visiting its commercial district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Providence's' is the US state whose capital it is, Rhode Island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rialto was Venice's mercantile exchange quarter, and the name is used for any commercial district.

clue.text: Four of these for bulls or bears

definitions.text: Four of these for bulls or bears

parts.words: Four of these for bulls or bears
parts.note: cattle are ruminants with a digestive system of four chambers, and 'bears' also hints at the verb sense, puts up with

explanation.surface: Seems to be stock-market talk of bulls and bears.
explanation.walkthrough: Bulls have four of these chambers; 'bears' doubles as a verb, since to bear something is to tolerate it in the same sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattle digest in four chambered bellies, and the word as a verb means tolerates or endures.

clue.text: Held by scout, uncivil servant's first to break out again

indicators.note: the uncivil and servant pieces are held inside the scouting word

parts.note: recce is short for reconnaissance, a scouting mission
rude means uncivil

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of servant's

explanation.surface: A rude servant captured by a scout makes another escape.
explanation.definitionFit: Recrudescence is a fresh outbreak, so the verb means to recur after a dormant spell, as a disease does.

clue.text: With exams due, worried friend needed problem solver

indicators.note: worried letters are disturbed and churned about into a new order

parts.note: china is Cockney rhyming slang for mate: china plate = mate

explanation.surface: A student anxious about exams needs a pal to help sort things out.
explanation.walkthrough: CHINA = friend is Cockney rhyming slang: 'china plate' rhymes with 'mate'.
explanation.definitionFit: In drama a god lowered by stage machinery to resolve the plot is a contrived device that settles every difficulty.

clue.text: One missing dog shakes partner

indicators.note: missing means the one letter is absent from the dog

parts.note: a collie is a sheepdog
one is the Roman numeral I
ague is a fever with shivering, the shakes

explanation.surface: A lost dog's owner trembles with worry over their companion.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-worker or associate is someone one works alongside, a partner in a job.

clue.text: Early Christian leaders still in seventh heaven

indicators.note: the leaders of the two words are their opening letters

parts.note: static means still, not moving

explanation.surface: The first Christian leaders are still in blissful paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Early Christian leaders' reads as church fathers but only gives two first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Seventh heaven is the highest bliss, so being there means being overjoyed or rapturous.

clue.text: One term in class without qualification

indicators.note: the one-and-term pieces go inside the word for class

parts.note: a category is a class or division
one is the Roman numeral I
to term something is to call or name it

explanation.surface: A school pupil spending a term in a class with no qualifications to show for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something categorically means saying it absolutely, with no reservations or hedging.

clue.text: Hear about contest for Gothic openwork

indicators.note: the hearing word goes about, around, the contest

parts.note: a judge tries a case, that is, hears it
a race is a contest

explanation.surface: Listening to a dispute over Gothic stone decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: The ornamental intersecting stone ribs of a Gothic window are patterned openwork.

clue.text: Turning blue before entering capital

indicators.note: the word for before enters the turned colour
turning means the colour word is read backwards

parts.note: navy is a dark blue
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Going pale blue before walking into a big city.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the capital city of Armenia.

clue.text: Catch 15 brought up short

indicators.note: in a down entry, brought up means read upwards, backwards
short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: the clue at 15 down is defined by partner

explanation.surface: Catching a colleague mentioned, but only briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: '15' stands for the definition of 15 down, partner, not its answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensnare someone is to catch them, in a trap or by trickery.

clue.text: Spooner here may get to Assam

definitions.text: Spooner here may get to Assam

parts.words: Spooner here may get to Assam
parts.note: not the Reverend Spooner: a spooner is simply someone using a spoon, and in this container a small spoon reaches the Indian leaves

explanation.surface: Seems to promise a Spoonerism, the Oxford don's famous sound-swapping slips.
explanation.walkthrough: No sounds are swapped: 'Spooner' means anyone wielding a caddy spoon, and Assam is a black tea from India.
explanation.definitionFit: A small box for storing loose tea leaves, from which one spoons out the Assam.

clue.text: Exhausted, having bottom pinched under a tree

indicators.note: in a down entry the shortened word sits under the letter a
pinched means stolen, so the bottom letter of the word is taken away

parts.note: spent means exhausted

explanation.surface: A weary walker, robbed of their wallet, slumped beneath a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A poplar with trembling leaves is a kind of tree.

clue.text: Currency in the news that makes for nervous transmission

clue.text: Back part is in federal area

clue.text: Dying, Home Guard's leader stops feast

clue.text: Japanese bread in stick that's spicy

clue.text: In competition be inclined to emulate Bowdler

indicators.note: the inclining word is placed in the word for competition

parts.note: a cup is a competition such as the FA Cup
